comment: Food questions (docs/TECHNICAL.md §8.7): what both platforms share as data. The web imports this file; Android's :core reads it as a resource. Texts for the model are English; texts for the user are in src/i18n.
requestPrompt: You turn a question about the user's own food log into a request for the app Blackwater Macros. The app computes every number from the log; you only choose what to compute.
Today is {today} ({weekday}). The user writes in {language} and usually logs foods in {language}.
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else.
Analyses (the "analysis" field) and the fields each one uses:
Leave out the fields an analysis does not use. Use "none" when the question is not about what the user ate (advice, recipes, targets, today's numbers, a photo) or when no analysis fits.
noneDescription: not about what the user ate
previousRequest: The previous request in this conversation was: {request}. For a follow-up ("and last month?", "and on weekends?") keep what it had and change only what the new question asks.

food_stats.description: how often and how much of a food the user eats, and the calories and macros it brings

ranking.description: the user's top foods by calories, protein, carbs, fat or how often they eat them

day_log.description: what the user ate on a day or a few days

compare.description: one number compared between weekdays and the weekend, or between two periods; of everything eaten, or of some foods when "foods" is given

food_vs_weight.description: how the user's weight moved with more or less of a food, or before and after a date ("since I stopped eating X")

fields.foods: search words for the food as the user may have logged it: the words of the question in the singular, synonyms, and the name in {language} and in English; at most 8. Example: chocolate milk → ["chocolate milk", "leche chocolatada", "chocolatada", "cacao"].
fields.from: the first day, "YYYY-MM-DD"; leave it out when the question names no period.
fields.to: the last day, "YYYY-MM-DD"; leave it out when the question names no period.
fields.split: "weekday_weekend", or "periods" to compare from–to with from2–to2.
fields.from2: the first day of the second period (split "periods").
fields.to2: the last day of the second period (split "periods").
fields.at: the day something changed ("since 1 October"), "YYYY-MM-DD"; leave it out when the question names none.

examples.question: How much chocolate milk do I drink?
What gives me most of my protein?
Do I eat more on weekends?
Did my weight change since I stopped drinking beer?
How much protein should I eat?

result.header: FOOD LOG RESULT, computed by the app from the user's log for the question above. Use these numbers as they are; do not recompute them or add others. Days without anything logged are not counted as zero.
result.period: Period: {from} to {to} ({days} days, {logged} with meals logged).
result.few: Only {logged} days with meals logged: present the numbers as a rough hint, not a firm average.
result.foodDays: Eaten {times} times in all, about {timesPerWeek} times a week, on {eatenDays} of the {logged} logged days (about {perWeek} days a week).
result.amount: Amount in {unit}: {total} {unit} in {entries} entries; {perEatenDay} {unit} per day it was eaten, {perLoggedDay} {unit} per logged day.
result.withoutAmount: {n} of the entries have no amount in g or ml, so they are left out of the amounts.
result.foodNutrition: These foods bring {calories} kcal per logged day ({share}% of the calories logged), {protein} g protein, {carbs} g carbs and {fat} g fat per logged day.
result.rankingTimesTitle: Top foods by how often they were eaten:
result.dayLogCut: Showing the last {shown} of the {days} days asked for.
result.macros: {calories} kcal, {protein} g protein, {carbs} g carbs, {fat} g fat
result.compareFoodsTitle: {metric} from these foods per logged day, compared:
result.compareTimesTitle: How often these foods were eaten, compared:
result.weightSplitStopped: The split is the day after the last time these foods were logged ({at}).
result.weightSplitStarted: The split is the first day these foods were logged ({at}).
result.weightSplitHalves: The split is the middle of the period ({at}): the foods were logged all along.
result.weightSplitAsked: The split is the day the user named ({at}).
result.weightFood: {label}: these foods on {eatenDays} of {logged} logged days, {calories} kcal from them per logged day; {total} kcal per logged day in all.
result.weightTrend: {label}: weight trend {rate} ± {margin} kg/week (from {weighIns} days with weigh-ins, compared only within weigh-ins taken alike).
result.weightTrendMissing: {label}: not enough weigh-ins for a trend (needs {minWeighIns} days with weigh-ins spanning {minSpan} days).
result.association: This shows an association, not a cause: other things changed too, such as the total calories above. Say so.
result.cut: (The rest was left out to keep this short.)
